value.overview: The Purplish-backed Quail-Dove is a secretive, ground-feeding dove of wet mountain forests in Costa Rica and western Panama. It is recognized by its purplish mantle, bluish-gray head and breast, white face and throat, dark facial markings, and warm brown wings. Usually seen alone or in pairs, it often walks or runs through dense vegetation rather than flying when disturbed. Its soft, distinctive song may be heard more often than the bird is seen.
value.classification: The Purplish-backed Quail-Dove belongs to the dove and pigeon family Columbidae and the genus Zentrygon. It is generally treated as a monotypic species.
value.identification: This medium-sized quail-dove is about 25–27 cm long. Adults have a grayish-white forehead, bluish-gray to greenish tones on the crown and neck, and a dull purplish back. The remaining upperparts are olive-brown with some reddish tones, while the wings become dark brown. The face and throat are white, marked by a black line through the eye and a dark malar stripe. The breast is slate-gray, the belly is pale buff to cinnamon, and the flanks are chocolate brown. The eye and surrounding bare skin are reddish or magenta.
value.rangeHabitat: The species is a resident of the mountains from Costa Rica into western and central Panama. In Costa Rica, it occurs from the Cordillera de Guanacaste in the north through suitable wet montane forests in the central and southeastern highlands. It inhabits cool, humid, dense forest, especially areas with thick understory and undisturbed ground cover. It is reported from roughly 400–800 m on some Caribbean slopes, at higher elevations in southeastern areas, and locally up to about 2,600 m.
value.migrationStatus: Resident in Costa Rica and Panama; no regular long-distance migration is known. Individuals may make local movements within mountain forests, but seasonal patterns are poorly documented.
value.breeding: In Costa Rica, breeding has been reported mainly from June through October. The nest is a loose, bulky cup or shallow bowl made from sticks and finer plant material, usually positioned in dense vegetation close to the ground. The species generally lays a single egg. Available information on incubation, parental care, and fledging is limited, and breeding behavior may vary between Costa Rica and Panama.
value.dietFeeding: The Purplish-backed Quail-Dove forages mainly on the forest floor, usually alone or in pairs. Its diet includes fallen fruit, seeds, insects, and worms. It searches through leaf litter and low vegetation, taking food from the ground. Dense, moist forest with a well-developed understory and abundant leaf litter provides important feeding habitat.
value.behavior: This quail-dove is shy and difficult to observe in dense forest. When alarmed, it commonly walks or runs away rather than immediately taking flight. If it does flush, it may fly to a higher perch or into nearby cover. Birds are usually encountered singly or in pairs. Its song is a soft, three-part phrase with the strongest emphasis on the final note, which can reveal its presence in thick vegetation.

conservation.populationTrend: The global population trend is not well quantified, but the species is described as locally fairly common in parts of its range.
